mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in the last two months signals a weakening in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of reduced consumer demand and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between HOUST drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last two months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity expands.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, suggests a stable monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for three months, or if the correlation between low inflation and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending is expected to rise.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both increase by more than 0.5% and 0.3% respectively in the last month, it signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint correlation between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
